title: 众人拾柴火焰高
subtitle: 森林里的暖冬晚会
origin: 民间谚语；根据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 每个人的一点付出都有价值；愿意求助、合理分工，能让合作更顺利。
moral.en: Every contribution matters. Asking for help and sharing tasks makes teamwork possible.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻大家共同出力，就能汇聚更大的力量。
idiomMeaning.en: Many people contributing together can achieve more than one person alone.

visualAnchor: Cozy snowy forest village square with timber cottages, bare birches and fir trees. Little Bear is a round cinnamon-brown bear with cream muzzle, mustard knitted scarf and teal sleeveless vest. Squirrel is a small russet squirrel with cream belly and plum scarf. Rabbit is a white rabbit with sky-blue jacket. Field Mouse is a tiny gray mouse with rust-red cap. Adult Badger is a tall gray badger in a brown wool coat. A wide low wooden shelter with forest-green canvas roof, log benches, and an enclosed iron stove operated only by Adult Badger; fire never handled by children.

pages.zh: 第一片雪花落在小熊手心里。森林的冬天来了。
pages.en: The first snowflake landed on Little Bear's paw. Winter had come to the forest.
pages.prompt: Wide forest village square; Little Bear studies first snowflakes on his outstretched paw, no other main characters.

pages.zh: “我们办场暖冬晚会吧！”小熊望着空空的广场，眼睛亮了。
pages.en: “Let's have a winter gathering!” Little Bear's eyes shone as he looked across the empty square.
pages.prompt: Bear imagines using the empty square, gestures joyfully toward open space, no thought bubbles.

pages.zh: 他答应搭好棚子、摆好座位，还要请獾伯伯生炉火。
pages.en: He promised to put up a shelter, arrange seats, and ask Mr. Badger to tend the stove.
pages.prompt: Bear and adult Badger inspect folded green canvas, logs and the cold enclosed stove.

pages.zh: 第二天，小熊拖来一根木头。木头真沉，雪地上留下一道长痕。
pages.en: The next day, he dragged over a log. It was heavy and left a long trail in the snow.
pages.prompt: Bear pulls one manageable log slowly on a rope along level snowy ground, close view of trail.

pages.zh: 小松鼠抱来几根细枝。“太少啦。”小熊摇摇头。
pages.en: Squirrel brought a few thin branches. “That's hardly any,” said Little Bear.
pages.prompt: Squirrel offers a small bundle of dry twigs, Bear looks doubtful beside large log pile.

pages.zh: 小兔想帮忙摆座位。“我自己来就好。”小熊又说。
pages.en: Rabbit offered to arrange the seats. “I can do it myself,” Little Bear replied.
pages.prompt: Rabbit gestures toward light bench pieces while Bear politely but stubbornly waves away help.

pages.zh: 棚顶的一角刚系好，另一角又滑下来。小熊跑来跑去，围巾都歪了。
pages.en: As soon as one corner of the roof was tied, another slipped loose. Little Bear hurried back and forth, his scarf crooked.
pages.prompt: Bear beneath partly assembled low shelter, loose green canvas corner hanging down, no climbing.

pages.zh: 太阳慢慢往下落，广场上还乱糟糟的。小熊坐在木头上，叹了口气。
pages.en: The sun sank lower, but the square was still a mess. Little Bear sat on a log and sighed.
pages.prompt: Quiet wide afternoon scene, tired Bear seated among scattered safe materials and unfinished shelter.

pages.zh: 一阵风吹过，没固定好的棚布鼓起来，又软软地落在雪地上。
pages.en: A gust lifted the loose canvas. It billowed, then settled softly onto the snow.
pages.prompt: Green canvas billows gently down onto empty snow beside Bear, no collapse or injury.

pages.zh: 小熊追过去，停住了。“原来，我一个人真的忙不过来。”
pages.en: Little Bear hurried after it, then stopped. “I really can't do all of this alone.”
pages.prompt: Bear holds edge of fallen canvas, small against the unfinished square, thoughtful expression.

pages.zh: 他找到伙伴们，红着脸说：“刚才对不起。你们还愿意帮我吗？”
pages.en: He found his friends. “I'm sorry about earlier. Would you still like to help?”
pages.prompt: Bear apologizes sincerely to Squirrel and Rabbit beside village cottages at sunset.

pages.zh: 大家围在一起商量。小熊搬木头，小兔安排座位，小松鼠收集干枝。
pages.en: Together they made a plan. Bear would move logs, Rabbit would arrange seats, and Squirrel would gather dry twigs.
pages.prompt: Friends gesture to separate material piles on level ground, clear collaborative planning, no written plan.

pages.zh: 獾伯伯检查支架，把棚顶牢牢固定好。“搭稳了，大家才安心。”
pages.en: Mr. Badger checked the supports and secured the roof. “A sturdy shelter keeps everyone comfortable.”
pages.prompt: Adult Badger secures final reachable shelter knot; children stand safely nearby holding light supplies.

pages.zh: 小田鼠也来了。“我能做什么呢？”他低头看见座位旁有个小坑。
pages.en: Field Mouse arrived too. “What can I do?” Looking down, he noticed a little hole beside a seat.
pages.prompt: Low viewpoint of tiny Mouse noticing a small shallow dip in the ground near a bench.

pages.zh: 他请大家绕开，找来小石子填平。再小的伙伴，也能帮上忙。
pages.en: He asked everyone to walk around it, then filled it with little stones. Even the smallest friend could help.
pages.prompt: Mouse carefully fills shallow dip with pebbles; Rabbit waits and smiles nearby.

pages.zh: 细枝一把又一把，渐渐堆满了篮子。小熊摸摸鼻子：“一点也不少呀。”
pages.en: Bundle by bundle, the twigs filled a basket. Little Bear smiled shyly. “That's quite a lot after all.”
pages.prompt: Squirrel shows now-full woven twig basket to humbled smiling Bear.

pages.zh: 獾伯伯独自照看炉火。孩子们隔着护栏，看暖光映上棚顶。
pages.en: Mr. Badger tended the stove himself. Behind the guardrail, the children watched warm light reach the roof.
pages.prompt: Adult Badger beside enclosed glowing stove with protective rail; children comfortably distant under secure shelter.

pages.zh: 小兔摆好座位，小松鼠挂好松果。晚会终于开始了！
pages.en: Rabbit finished the seats, and Squirrel hung the pinecones. The gathering was ready at last!
pages.prompt: Festive completed shelter with pinecone garlands, log benches, animals arriving in warm dusk light.

pages.zh: 小熊举起热汤碗：“谢谢你们。这个晚会，是我们一起办成的。”
pages.en: Little Bear raised his bowl of warm soup. “Thank you. We made this gathering happen together.”
pages.prompt: Bear addresses seated friends holding safe warm soup bowls, adults supervise stove in background.

pages.zh: 雪花还在飘，棚子里却暖融融的。众人拾柴火焰高，小小的付出汇成了大大的温暖。
pages.en: Snow still drifted outside, but the shelter was cozy. Many small contributions had made a wonderful, warm evening.
pages.prompt: Wide final shelter glowing amid snowy village, all five fixed characters sharing peaceful gathering, enclosed stove behind rail.

title: 心急吃不了热豆腐
subtitle: 小狐狸的第一家豆腐摊
origin: 民间谚语；根据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 耐心不是什么都不做；等待时，也可以准备下一件事。
moral.en: Patience can be active: use waiting time to prepare for what comes next.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻做事不能一味着急，有些步骤和等待是必要的。
idiomMeaning.en: Rushing cannot replace the steps and time a task needs.

visualAnchor: Rustic woodland tofu kitchen and village market, warm wood counters, ceramic bowls, wooden tofu press, bamboo trays. Little Fox is a small orange fox with cream cheeks, white tail tip, sage-green apron. Grandma Fox is an older silver-orange fox with round spectacles and indigo apron. Duck customer is a pale-yellow duck in blue vest. Grandma alone handles stove, hot soy milk and heavy grinding equipment; Fox helps with cool ingredients and table setting.

pages.zh: 集市快开了，小狐狸想跟奶奶一起摆个豆腐摊。
pages.en: Market day was coming. Little Fox wanted to run a tofu stall with Grandma.
pages.prompt: Establish cozy woodland kitchen; Fox and Grandma beside empty bamboo serving trays.

pages.zh: “我要做又白又嫩的豆腐！”他洗好手，系紧了小围裙。
pages.en: “I'll make soft, snowy-white tofu!” He washed his paws and tied his apron.
pages.prompt: Fox ties sage apron beside washbasin, Grandma smiles at clean wooden counter.

pages.zh: 奶奶把黄豆泡进水里。“先让豆子慢慢吸足水。”
pages.en: Grandma soaked the soybeans. “First, they need time to take in water.”
pages.prompt: Grandma pours cool water into ceramic bowl of dry yellow soybeans; Fox watches.

pages.zh: 没过多久，小狐狸就捧起豆碗：“现在可以磨了吗？”
pages.en: Before long, Little Fox picked up the bowl. “Can we grind them now?”
pages.prompt: Eager Fox holding bowl with still-small beans toward patient Grandma.

pages.zh: 奶奶让他捏捏豆子。硬硬的豆心，还没有泡透呢。
pages.en: Grandma let him squeeze a bean. Its hard middle was not ready yet.
pages.prompt: Close view of Fox gently examining one soaked but still firm bean over bowl, no biting.

pages.zh: 豆子终于泡好了。奶奶磨浆、煮浆，小狐狸在旁边准备干净的布。
pages.en: When the beans were ready, Grandma ground and cooked them. Little Fox prepared clean cloths nearby.
pages.prompt: Grandma safely manages steaming pot in back; Fox folds clean cloths on separate cool counter.

pages.zh: 豆浆点好后，慢慢结成豆花。小狐狸趴在桌边，急得尾巴直摇。
pages.en: The prepared soy milk slowly formed soft curds. Little Fox watched, his tail swishing impatiently.
pages.prompt: Fox watches covered curd bowl from safe distance at table; Grandma nearby, warm steam subtle.

pages.zh: 奶奶把豆花放进模具压好。他却提早打开，豆腐一下散了边。
pages.en: Grandma put the curds in a press. He opened it too soon, and the edges crumbled.
pages.prompt: Fox opens small wooden press on cool counter too early; soft curd edges slump, Grandma observes calmly.

pages.zh: 远处传来集市的笑声。小狐狸低下头：“我们是不是来不及了？”
pages.en: Laughter drifted in from the market. Little Fox lowered his head. “Are we too late?”
pages.prompt: Fox slumps by crumbly tofu tray; colorful market seen through kitchen window.

pages.zh: “这一份可以做豆腐羹。”奶奶说，“下一份，我们按步骤来。”
pages.en: “This batch can become tofu soup,” Grandma said. “Let's give the next one the time it needs.”
pages.prompt: Grandma kindly indicates bowl for crumbled tofu and a second prepared curd batch, no waste.

pages.zh: 重新压好豆腐，小狐狸忍住没掀盖子。“等待的时候，我能做什么？”
pages.en: With the next batch pressed, Little Fox left the lid alone. “What can I do while we wait?”
pages.prompt: Fox pulls paws back from securely closed tofu press and looks thoughtfully at Grandma.

pages.zh: 他把小碗洗干净，一只一只摆在托盘上。
pages.en: He washed the bowls and arranged them neatly on a tray.
pages.prompt: Fox washing and lining up ceramic bowls at cool basin with playful reflections.

pages.zh: 他又擦好桌子，摆好勺子，还给客人留出舒服的位置。
pages.en: Then he wiped the table, set out spoons, and made room for the customers.
pages.prompt: Fox setting low market table with bowls and spoons, stall now organized.

pages.zh: 奶奶揭开模具，白白的豆腐稳稳当当地躺在里面。
pages.en: Grandma opened the press. A smooth white block of tofu rested inside.
pages.prompt: Grandma reveals neatly formed tofu in wooden mold while Fox beams.

pages.zh: 第一位客人来了！小狐狸端来小碗，奶奶盛好热豆腐。
pages.en: Their first customer arrived! Little Fox brought a bowl, and Grandma served the hot tofu.
pages.prompt: Duck customer seated at stall; Fox supplies empty bowl and Grandma ladles tofu safely.

pages.zh: 小狐狸也想立刻尝一口。热气扑上来，他赶紧停住，轻轻吹了吹。
pages.en: Little Fox wanted a taste right away. Feeling the steam, he paused and blew gently.
pages.prompt: Fox seated with spoon held well away from mouth blowing on warm tofu, Grandma nearby.

pages.zh: “原来，做好要等一等，吃的时候也要等一等。”他笑了。
pages.en: “Making it takes patience, and tasting it does too,” he said with a smile.
pages.prompt: Fox and Grandma share gentle laugh beside ready tofu tray in market light.

pages.zh: 集市上，第一碗豆腐慢慢吃完了。小狐狸不再催，因为好滋味值得等。
pages.en: At the market, the first bowl was slowly enjoyed. Little Fox no longer hurried. Some good things need time.
pages.prompt: Warm closing market stall, relaxed Fox seated with Grandma and Duck, tidy used bowls, no crowd urgency.

title: 一分耕耘，一分收获
subtitle: 小兔的歪歪胡萝卜
origin: 民间谚语；根据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 认真付出、不断学习，收获不只是一场比赛的名次。
moral.en: Careful effort and learning bring rewards beyond winning a prize.

idiomMeaning.zh: 付出劳动，才有获得成果的基础；收获也受方法、条件和时间影响。
idiomMeaning.en: Effort lays the groundwork for a harvest, alongside good methods, conditions, and time.

visualAnchor: Sunny temperate woodland allotment with low wooden fence and small timber shed; Little Rabbit is a cream-white rabbit with one floppy left ear, sky-blue overalls and straw sunhat; Neighbor Goat is an adult gentle beige goat with short horns and olive apron. Fixed red watering can, shallow wicker harvest basket, carrot beds and small drainage ditch. Seasons progress from spring to golden autumn, green carrot tops never mistaken for orange fruit above ground.

pages.zh: 春天，小兔看见集市上的大胡萝卜，羡慕得耳朵都竖起来了。
pages.en: One spring day, Little Rabbit admired the huge carrots at the market. His ears perked up.
pages.prompt: Rabbit admires giant harvested carrots displayed on village market stall in spring.

pages.zh: “秋天，我也要带最大的胡萝卜来！”他抱回一包种子。
pages.en: “In autumn, I'll bring the biggest carrot too!” He carried home a packet of seeds.
pages.prompt: Rabbit carries plain unlettered seed packet toward empty fenced garden, excited stride.

pages.zh: 他翻松一小块地，把种子撒下去，再盖上薄薄的土。
pages.en: He loosened a small patch of earth, sowed the seeds, and covered them lightly.
pages.prompt: Rabbit carefully sows tiny seeds in prepared spring bed, small hand tool beside him.

pages.zh: 每天，他都提来满满一壶水，浇呀浇，盼着胡萝卜快点长大。
pages.en: Every day, he brought a full watering can and watered eagerly, hoping the carrots would grow quickly.
pages.prompt: Rabbit pours too much water onto small seedling bed, visible puddle but no flooding.

pages.zh: 小苗冒出来了，可有的挤在一起，有的叶子软软地垂着。
pages.en: Seedlings appeared, but some were crowded together and others had drooping leaves.
pages.prompt: Low garden close-up of crowded seedlings and drooping tops, Rabbit crouches puzzled.

pages.zh: 小兔急忙找山羊邻居：“我天天浇水，怎么还长不好呢？”
pages.en: Little Rabbit asked his neighbor Goat, “I water every day. Why aren't they growing well?”
pages.prompt: Rabbit shows red watering can to adult Goat at fence, concerned expression.

pages.zh: 山羊捏捏湿土，又指指杂草：“先看看，它们真正需要什么。”
pages.en: Goat felt the wet soil and pointed to the weeds. “First, let's see what they actually need.”
pages.prompt: Goat kneels examining damp soil and weeds while Rabbit listens attentively.

pages.zh: 他们拔掉杂草，给挤在一起的小苗腾出地方。阳光照进了菜畦。
pages.en: They removed weeds and thinned the crowded seedlings. Sunlight reached the bed.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and Goat carefully weed and thin seedlings, newly spaced rows visible.

pages.zh: 小兔不再只顾浇水。他摸摸土、看看叶子，再决定怎样照料。
pages.en: Little Rabbit stopped watering without looking. He checked the soil and leaves before deciding what to do.
pages.prompt: Rabbit checks soil with fingertips beside watering can, healthy carrot tops behind.

pages.zh: 一天、两天，菜叶舒展开来。小兔的小本子里，多了许多观察图。
pages.en: Day by day, the leaves spread out. His little notebook filled with sketches of what he noticed.
pages.prompt: Rabbit sketches simple leaf shapes in notebook, thriving garden beyond, no legible words.

pages.zh: 夏天的一场大雨，把菜畦冲出几道沟。有几棵小苗歪倒了。
pages.en: A summer downpour cut little channels through the bed. A few plants leaned over.
pages.prompt: After-rain garden with shallow runoff channels and tilted seedlings, Rabbit watches from dry path.

pages.zh: 小兔看着满地泥水，鼻子一酸：“我的胡萝卜是不是全没了？”
pages.en: Looking at the muddy bed, Little Rabbit sniffled. “Have I lost all my carrots?”
pages.prompt: Rabbit crouches sadly beside muddy garden, no severe storm, soft overcast light.

pages.zh: 雨停后，山羊陪他查看。大部分根还好，只是需要排水和扶正。
pages.en: When the rain stopped, Goat checked with him. Most roots were fine; the bed needed drainage and care.
pages.prompt: Goat gently checks base of tilted carrot plant with Rabbit, hopeful expressions.

pages.zh: 他们疏通小沟，扶好幼苗，又把松掉的泥土轻轻拢回来。
pages.en: They cleared the little ditch, straightened the seedlings, and gently firmed the loose soil.
pages.prompt: Goat clears shallow drainage channel while Rabbit firms soil around upright seedling.

pages.zh: 太阳重新出来。小兔每天来看一看，也学会了等一等。
pages.en: The sun returned. Little Rabbit checked each day and learned to give the plants time.
pages.prompt: Rabbit quietly observes growing lush tops from garden path under warm late summer sun.

pages.zh: 秋天到了！他拔出第一根胡萝卜——弯弯的，像一只小月牙。
pages.en: Autumn arrived! His first carrot was curved like a little crescent moon.
pages.prompt: Rabbit proudly lifts one curved orange carrot from soil, golden autumn foliage.

pages.zh: 第二根短短的，第三根胖胖的。很快，篮子就装满了。
pages.en: The next was short, and another was plump. Soon his basket was full.
pages.prompt: Rabbit beside wicker basket full of varied short plump curved carrots, harvested garden.

pages.zh: 集市上，最大的胡萝卜奖给了别人。小兔失落了一会儿，又低头看看自己的篮子。
pages.en: At the market, someone else won the biggest-carrot prize. Little Rabbit felt disappointed, then looked at his own basket.
pages.prompt: Rabbit holding varied harvest watches large winning carrot with simple blank rosette on separate stall.

pages.zh: “这一篮，是我照料出来的。”他挑出几根，邀请山羊一起煮汤。
pages.en: “I helped this whole basket grow.” He chose some carrots and invited Goat to make soup together.
pages.prompt: Rabbit offers carrots and invitation to Goat beside garden gate, proud gentle smile.

pages.zh: 热汤香香的。小兔尝到收获的甜，也记住了泥土里学来的本领。
pages.en: The soup smelled wonderful. Little Rabbit tasted his harvest and remembered all the skills he had learned.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and Goat share warm soup at rustic table, varied carrots in basket, golden garden through window.

title: 远亲不如近邻
subtitle: 小獾搬家的第一场雨
origin: 民间谚语；根据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 珍惜远方的亲情，也主动认识和关心身边的人。
moral.en: Cherish distant relatives while getting to know and caring for nearby neighbors.

idiomMeaning.zh: 亲人住得远时，身边的邻居往往能更及时地相互照应。
idiomMeaning.en: Nearby neighbors can often offer timely help when relatives live far away.

visualAnchor: Welcoming woodland lane with rounded timber cottages, low fences and broad safe paths. Little Badger has soft gray fur with two black face stripes, rust-orange cardigan and small green satchel. Deer neighbor is a slim tan deer with white spots and teal shawl, no antlers. Adult Beaver carpenter has brown fur, broad flat tail, indigo work apron. Rabbit neighbor is cream-white with plum dress. Cousin Badger is a taller gray badger with identical family face stripes and sky-blue waistcoat. Little Badger never climbs roof; adult Beaver alone repairs it after rain stops.

pages.zh: 小獾搬进了林间小屋。窗前有一条陌生的小路，远处是青色的山。
pages.en: Little Badger moved into a woodland cottage. An unfamiliar lane lay outside, with blue hills beyond.
pages.prompt: Wide establishing cottage and woodland lane, Badger with moving basket looking toward distant hills.

pages.zh: 他把和表哥的画像摆好，轻轻说：“要是你也住在这里就好了。”
pages.en: He set out a portrait of himself with his cousin. “I wish you lived here too,” he whispered.
pages.prompt: Badger gently places simple family portrait on shelf inside sparse cottage, wistful mood.

pages.zh: 小鹿经过篱笆，笑着打招呼。小獾点点头，又低头整理箱子。
pages.en: Deer waved from the fence. Little Badger nodded, then returned to unpacking.
pages.prompt: Deer greets from low fence while Badger distractedly sorts wooden moving boxes.

pages.zh: 小兔送来一小篮面包。他道了谢，却不知道还能说些什么。
pages.en: Rabbit brought a little basket of bread. He thanked her, unsure what else to say.
pages.prompt: Rabbit offers bread basket at cottage doorway; Badger shyly receives it.

pages.zh: 傍晚，乌云越过山头。小獾关好窗，听见屋里“滴答”一声。
pages.en: At dusk, clouds rolled over the hills. Little Badger shut the window and heard a drip indoors.
pages.prompt: Badger closes window as first water droplet falls from small ceiling seam, soft cloudy dusk.

pages.zh: 一滴，两滴，雨水落在桌角。他连忙拿碗接住，旁边却又漏了起来。
pages.en: Drip, drip. Rain landed on the table. He caught it in a bowl, but another spot began to leak.
pages.prompt: Badger arranges small bowls below two minor leaks, dry room majority visible.

pages.zh: 小獾给表哥写信：“屋顶漏雨了，你能来帮我吗？”
pages.en: Little Badger wrote to his cousin. “My roof is leaking. Can you help?”
pages.prompt: Badger writing letter at dry desk beside bowls, paper blank to viewer, no rendered letters.

pages.zh: 可邮差明早才来，表哥还住在山那边。信寄出去，也不能立刻收到回音。
pages.en: But the post would not leave until morning, and his cousin lived beyond the hills. A reply would take time.
pages.prompt: Badger holds closed envelope at window gazing across darkening distant hills and empty lane.

pages.zh: 他抱着湿了一角的毯子，站在门口，不知道该怎么办。
pages.en: Holding a blanket with one damp corner, he stood in the doorway, unsure what to do.
pages.prompt: Badger at sheltered doorway holding folded slightly damp blanket, gentle rain outside.

pages.zh: 小鹿看见了，赶紧拿来大水桶：“先接住水，别让地板更湿了。”
pages.en: Deer noticed and brought a large bucket. “Let's catch the water before it spreads.”
pages.prompt: Deer carries empty wooden bucket to Badger's sheltered doorway, helpful posture.

pages.zh: 小兔招招手：“今晚先来我家吃饭吧，那里暖和又干燥。”
pages.en: Rabbit waved. “Come eat at my house tonight. It's warm and dry.”
pages.prompt: Rabbit welcomes Badger and Deer through nearby warmly lit cottage door under shared umbrella.

pages.zh: 河狸师傅听说后，带来工具：“等雨停了，我来检查屋顶。”
pages.en: When Beaver heard, he brought his tools. “Once the rain stops, I'll check your roof.”
pages.prompt: Adult Beaver with closed toolbox talks with neighbors indoors, rainfall visible outside, no roof work yet.

pages.zh: 第二天放晴，河狸师傅补好屋顶。小獾在地面递材料，小鹿帮忙收拾屋里。
pages.en: The next day was clear. Beaver repaired the roof while Badger passed supplies from the ground and Deer tidied indoors.
pages.prompt: Adult Beaver securely on low roof repairing shingles, Badger safely on ground with materials, Deer at doorway.

pages.zh: 小獾擦干最后一块地板。原来，这条陌生的小路上，住着这么热心的人。
pages.en: Little Badger dried the last patch of floor. This unfamiliar lane was full of caring neighbors.
pages.prompt: Badger drying clean floor, open door frames friendly neighbors and sunny lane.

pages.zh: 过了几天，他看见小鹿提着两只沉篮子，主动跑过去接了一只。
pages.en: A few days later, he saw Deer carrying two heavy baskets and hurried over to take one.
pages.prompt: Badger and Deer walking level lane each carrying one basket, relaxed conversation.

pages.zh: 小兔出门时，他也记得帮她给窗边的花浇水。
pages.en: When Rabbit went out, he remembered to water the flowers by her window.
pages.prompt: Badger gently waters Rabbit's window-box flowers from ground, sunny cottage wall.

pages.zh: 周末，表哥来做客。“屋顶好啦？”“嗯，多亏了我的邻居！”
pages.en: His cousin visited that weekend. “The roof is fixed?” “Yes, thanks to my neighbors!”
pages.prompt: Cousin Badger with small travel bag admires repaired cottage while Little Badger welcomes him.

pages.zh: 小獾带表哥走过小路，一扇扇门都打开了。远方有亲人，身边也有温暖的照应。
pages.en: Little Badger introduced his cousin along the lane. Doors opened in welcome. He had family far away and kindness close by.
pages.prompt: Final sunny lane with both badgers greeted by Deer, Rabbit and Beaver at adjoining cottages.

title: 赠人玫瑰，手有余香
subtitle: 小刺猬的最后一朵花
origin: 民间谚语；根据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 善意不是交换礼物的条件；关心别人，也可以保留自己珍爱的东西。
moral.en: Kindness is not a bargain for gifts, and caring for others can include caring for yourself.

idiomMeaning.zh: 帮助别人、分享善意时，自己也能感受到快乐和温暖。
idiomMeaning.en: Giving kindness can bring warmth and happiness to the giver too.

visualAnchor: Gentle spring woodland garden and cozy round cottage. Little Hedgehog is small with soft chestnut spines, cream face, tiny round ears and moss-green knitted cardigan. Duckling is pale yellow with pale-blue scarf. Aunt Goat is adult cream goat with lilac shawl. Mouse friend is gray with faded blue fabric hat. Rose garden has pink thornless garden roses, shallow oval wicker flower basket and a simple small birthday table. No sharp tools in child paws; flowers are prepared stems.

pages.zh: 小刺猬的生日快到了。院子里的粉红玫瑰，也一朵朵开了。
pages.en: Little Hedgehog's birthday was coming, and pink roses were opening in his garden.
pages.prompt: Establish Hedgehog admiring blooming pink roses outside round woodland cottage.

pages.zh: 他想把花摆满小桌子，请朋友们来吃点心。
pages.en: He wanted to fill his little table with flowers and invite friends for treats.
pages.prompt: Hedgehog plans arrangement beside bare birthday table by garden window, empty vases.

pages.zh: 清早，他装好一篮花，沿着小路去邀请大家。
pages.en: Early one morning, he took a basket of flowers and went to invite everyone.
pages.prompt: Hedgehog walks sunny woodland path carrying oval basket of prepared pink roses.

pages.zh: 池塘边，小鸭望着远方。“我有点想家，那边也开着这样的花。”
pages.en: By the pond, Duckling gazed into the distance. “I miss home. Flowers like these grow there too.”
pages.prompt: Duckling sits safely on dry grass beside pond, Hedgehog pauses with basket.

pages.zh: 小刺猬挑出一朵：“送给你，让它陪你想一想家。”
pages.en: Little Hedgehog chose a rose. “This is for you. It can keep you company while you think of home.”
pages.prompt: Hedgehog gently offers one thornless pink rose to wistful Duckling.

pages.zh: 走到山羊阿姨家，他看见窗帘半掩着，屋里静悄悄的。
pages.en: At Aunt Goat's house, the curtains were half closed and everything was quiet.
pages.prompt: Hedgehog with basket stands outside cozy cottage with partly drawn curtains.

pages.zh: 阿姨正照顾休养的家人。小刺猬轻声说：“这些花，放在窗边好吗？”
pages.en: Aunt Goat was caring for a resting relative. “Could these flowers go by the window?” Hedgehog asked softly.
pages.prompt: Aunt Goat receives small rose bouquet at doorway, resting relative only softly suggested by distant blanket.

pages.zh: 粉红的花映着阳光，安静的房间多了一点春天。
pages.en: Sunlight touched the pink petals, bringing a little spring into the quiet room.
pages.prompt: Close warm window still life of roses in vase, Aunt Goat and Hedgehog smiling softly nearby.

pages.zh: 转过弯，他遇见小老鼠。那顶旧帽子的边上，缝着一块补丁。
pages.en: Around the bend, he met Mouse. A patch covered one side of Mouse's old hat.
pages.prompt: Mouse adjusts faded blue patched hat beside garden fence, Hedgehog notices kindly.

pages.zh: “我很喜欢这顶帽子。”小老鼠说。小刺猬问：“要不要添一朵花？”
pages.en: “I love this hat,” Mouse said. “Would you like a flower for it?” asked Hedgehog.
pages.prompt: Hedgehog asks permission while holding a pink rose near but not touching Mouse's hat.

pages.zh: 小老鼠点点头。花别好了，旧帽子变得像一个小花园。
pages.en: Mouse nodded. With the flower tucked in, the old hat looked like a tiny garden.
pages.prompt: Mouse proudly wears patched blue hat with single pink rose, Hedgehog delighted.

pages.zh: 回家的时候，篮子里只剩最后一朵。小刺猬的脚步慢了下来。
pages.en: On the way home, only one flower remained. Little Hedgehog slowed his steps.
pages.prompt: Hedgehog looks into nearly empty wicker basket containing exactly one rose on quiet path.

pages.zh: 他看看空空的小桌子，心里有一点舍不得：“我的花桌子没有了。”
pages.en: He looked at his empty table and felt a little sad. “There goes my table full of flowers.”
pages.prompt: Hedgehog beside plain table holding single rose, wistful but gentle mood.

pages.zh: 想了一会儿，他把最后一朵插进小瓶。“这一朵，留给我自己。”
pages.en: After a moment, he put the last rose in a little vase. “This one is for me.”
pages.prompt: Hedgehog carefully places single pink rose in small glass vase at table center.

pages.zh: 生日那天，小鸭来了，带着一张家乡的画，讲起花田旁的小屋。
pages.en: On his birthday, Duckling came with a picture of home and stories of a cottage beside a flower field.
pages.prompt: Duckling shows wordless watercolor of flower field and cottage to Hedgehog at birthday table.

pages.zh: 山羊阿姨也来坐了一会儿：“你送的花，让我们的窗边亮了好几天。”
pages.en: Aunt Goat stopped by. “Your flowers brightened our window for days,” she said.
pages.prompt: Aunt Goat chats warmly with Hedgehog and Duckling beside simple snacks and single rose.

pages.zh: 小老鼠戴着花帽子，逗得大家哈哈笑。小桌子周围，渐渐坐满了朋友。
pages.en: Mouse arrived in the flowered hat and made everyone laugh. Friends filled the seats around the table.
pages.prompt: Mouse in fixed rose hat joins Goat Duckling Hedgehog at small table, joyful relaxed laughter.

pages.zh: 桌上只有一朵玫瑰，屋里却满是笑声。小刺猬闻闻手心，好像还留着花香。
pages.en: There was only one rose on the table, but the room was full of laughter. Hedgehog's paws seemed to hold its scent.
pages.prompt: Intimate final scene Hedgehog gently smells paw beside single rose vase, friends softly framed around table.

title: 吃一堑，长一智
subtitle: 小猴的南瓜运输队
origin: 民间谚语；根据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 犯错后别只责怪自己；找到原因，试着改进，经验才会变成本领。
moral.en: After a mistake, look for causes and try improvements rather than only blaming yourself.

idiomMeaning.zh: 经历一次挫折，认真总结原因，就能增长经验和见识。
idiomMeaning.en: A setback can teach us something when we examine it and change our approach.

visualAnchor: Friendly woodland vegetable farm, level dirt lane with broad curve and a village market. Little Monkey is a small golden-brown monkey with cream muzzle, red neckerchief and teal short overalls. Rabbit helper is white with mustard vest. Adult Donkey farmer is gray with indigo apron. Fixed small wooden two-wheel handcart with tan handles; initially no sideboards, later sturdy low sideboards and canvas straps. Orange pumpkins vary in size; fallen pumpkins never hit anyone.

pages.zh: 农场的南瓜成熟了。小猴自告奋勇，要帮驴伯伯送到集市去。
pages.en: The pumpkins were ripe. Little Monkey volunteered to take them to the market for Farmer Donkey.
pages.prompt: Wide pumpkin farm; Monkey raises paw eagerly beside Donkey and empty low wooden handcart.

pages.zh: 他推来小木车：“多装一点，就能少跑几趟！”
pages.en: He brought a little wooden cart. “If I load more, I can make fewer trips!”
pages.prompt: Monkey cheerfully points from large pumpkin pile to small cart, Donkey nearby.

pages.zh: 南瓜一层叠一层，堆得比车把还高。小猴踮脚，才看得见前面的路。
pages.en: He stacked pumpkins above the handles. He had to stand on tiptoe to see ahead.
pages.prompt: Overloaded stationary cart with pumpkins obscuring Monkey's view, no movement yet.

pages.zh: 刚走一段，车轮碰到小石头。咕噜噜，几个南瓜滚到了草地上。
pages.en: Soon a wheel bumped a stone. Several pumpkins rolled onto the grass.
pages.prompt: Cart wheel meets small stone on level path, pumpkins gently roll onto empty grassy verge.

pages.zh: 幸好没有碰到谁。小猴停好车，红着脸把南瓜一只只捡回来。
pages.en: Luckily, nobody was in the way. Little Monkey stopped and gathered the pumpkins, his cheeks warm.
pages.prompt: Monkey safely parks cart and collects intact pumpkins from soft grass, sheepish expression.

pages.zh: “刚才一定是没摆整齐。”他又把南瓜堆高，这次摆得特别齐。
pages.en: “They must have been untidy,” he thought. He stacked them high again, this time in neat rows.
pages.prompt: Monkey carefully arranges too-high neat pumpkin stack in stationary cart.

pages.zh: 来到弯道，他一转车把，最上面的南瓜又慢慢滑了下去。
pages.en: At the bend, he turned the handles. A pumpkin slid from the top once more.
pages.prompt: At broad level curve one top pumpkin gently slips onto empty grass, Monkey looks surprised.

pages.zh: 小猴坐在路边，气得抓耳朵：“我是不是根本不会运东西？”
pages.en: Little Monkey sat beside the path. “Am I simply no good at carrying things?”
pages.prompt: Monkey seated on safe grassy verge away from parked cart, frustrated lowered head.

pages.zh: 小兔赶来帮忙，没有笑他。“我们先看看，是哪里出了问题。”
pages.en: Rabbit came to help without laughing. “Let's see what went wrong.”
pages.prompt: Rabbit sits kindly beside Monkey, both look toward stationary loaded cart.

pages.zh: 他们蹲下看车轮，又绕着车走了一圈。小猴发现，车边连挡板也没有。
pages.en: They checked the wheels and walked around the cart. Monkey noticed it had no sideboards.
pages.prompt: Monkey and Rabbit inspect exposed flat cart edges and wheels while safely parked.

pages.zh: “装得高，容易晃；没有挡板，南瓜就容易滚出去。”小猴说。
pages.en: “A tall stack wobbles, and without sides the pumpkins can roll off,” Monkey said.
pages.prompt: Monkey points to top-heavy stack and open cart edge, Rabbit listens, no text diagrams.

pages.zh: 小兔又指指弯道：“这条路不太平，转弯也不能太急。”
pages.en: Rabbit pointed at the bend. “The path is uneven, and we need to turn slowly.”
pages.prompt: Rabbit gestures toward small stones and broad bend ahead, cart in background.

pages.zh: 他们回到农场，请驴伯伯给小车装上结实的挡板。
pages.en: Back at the farm, they asked Farmer Donkey to add sturdy sides to the cart.
pages.prompt: Adult Donkey fits wooden sideboards in workshop; Monkey Rabbit watch from safe distance, tools adult-only.

pages.zh: 这一次，小猴只装了低低一层，再和伯伯一起固定好。
pages.en: This time, Monkey loaded just one low layer and helped Donkey secure it.
pages.prompt: Monkey and Donkey secure single low pumpkin layer with canvas straps inside newly sided cart.

pages.zh: 出发前，他们先看路，避开石头多的地方，选了一条平缓的小道。
pages.en: Before leaving, they checked the route and chose a smoother path with fewer stones.
pages.prompt: Monkey and Rabbit scout two visible paths and choose smoother level lane, Donkey by cart.

pages.zh: 小猴慢慢推，小兔在旁边照应。到了弯道，他们一起放慢脚步。
pages.en: Monkey pushed steadily, with Rabbit beside him. At the bend, they both slowed down.
pages.prompt: Friends carefully guide securely loaded cart around broad gentle curve, calm movement.

pages.zh: 这回，南瓜稳稳地到了集市。小猴摸摸挡板，终于笑了。
pages.en: This time, the pumpkins arrived safely. Monkey patted a sideboard and smiled.
pages.prompt: Monkey and Rabbit arrive at market with intact secured pumpkin load, relieved joy.

pages.zh: 剩下的南瓜，他们分几趟送完。多走了些路，却没有再来回捡南瓜。
pages.en: They delivered the rest in several trips. It meant more walking, but no chasing fallen pumpkins.
pages.prompt: Later farm scene last modest pumpkin batch loaded, tidy emptied harvest pile, late afternoon.

pages.zh: 过了几天，农场要运苹果。小猴没有急着装车，先检查轮子和挡板。
pages.en: A few days later, apples needed delivering. Monkey checked the wheels and sides before loading.
pages.prompt: Monkey checks wheel and sideboard beside stacked apple baskets at farm.

pages.zh: 他还问：“苹果怎么放更稳？”吃一堑，长一智，这次他带上了新学会的办法。
pages.en: “How can we keep the apples steady?” he asked. His setback had become a lesson he could use.
pages.prompt: Monkey and Donkey arrange apples in shallow secured baskets inside fixed cart, Rabbit helps, hopeful ending.

title: 千里之行，始于足下
subtitle: 小蜗牛去看海
origin: 语出《老子》第六十四章；本书为依据成语寓意创作的原创童话。

moral.zh: 把大目标分成小步骤；可以休息、问路，也可以调整计划。
moral.en: Break a large goal into smaller steps, with room for rest, help, and changes of plan.

idiomMeaning.zh: 走很远的路，也要从脚下第一步开始；比喻大事要从眼前的小事做起。
idiomMeaning.en: A long journey begins with the first step; large goals start with small actions.

visualAnchor: Gentle miniature woodland-to-coast journey through meadow, shallow stream with maintained footbridge, broad low hill path, sheltered hollow log and safe sand dunes. Little Snail has golden-ochre skin, dark round eyes on two antennae, warm chestnut spiral shell with one cream band and a tiny teal travel satchel. Grandma Snail has pale-ochre skin, gray-brown shell and lilac scarf. Ladybird friend is red with seven black spots. Turtle guide has moss-green shell and ochre scarf. Seagull guide is white with gray wings. No dangerous heights; snail stays on dry land.

pages.zh: 小蜗牛捧着一枚贝壳，听见里面轻轻的声音。“大海真的这样响吗？”
pages.en: Little Snail held a seashell and heard a soft sound. “Does the sea really sound like this?”
pages.prompt: Snail in woodland home listening to small seashell, warm morning close-up.

pages.zh: 奶奶笑了：“那是贝壳让周围的声音变得不一样。真正的大海，要亲耳听。”
pages.en: Grandma smiled. “The shell changes the sounds around us. To hear the real sea, you'll need to go there.”
pages.prompt: Grandma and Snail discuss seashell beside open window with distant blue horizon, no magical shell.

pages.zh: 小蜗牛展开地图。从家到海边，路线长得绕过了半张桌子。
pages.en: Little Snail unfolded a map. The route to the sea stretched across half the table.
pages.prompt: Tiny Snail studies large wordless pictorial route map across low table, daunting scale.

pages.zh: “这么远，我什么时候才能到呀？”他把小包又放了下来。
pages.en: “It's so far. How will I ever get there?” He put his little bag down again.
pages.prompt: Snail lowers teal satchel beside map, discouraged antennae tilted downward.

pages.zh: 奶奶指着窗外：“今天，先走到村口那棵大树，好不好？”
pages.en: Grandma pointed outside. “Today, how about just reaching the big tree at the edge of the village?”
pages.prompt: Grandma indicates nearby large tree through window, Snail follows her gaze.

pages.zh: 清晨，小蜗牛背好包，慢慢滑过门前的一块石头。旅程开始了。
pages.en: In the morning, Little Snail put on his bag and crossed the stone outside. His journey had begun.
pages.prompt: Low close view Snail with teal satchel moving over smooth doorstep stone into dawn light.

pages.zh: 到了大树下，他回头看。家已经小了一点点，原来自己真的走出来了！
pages.en: At the tree, he looked back. Home was a little smaller. He really had started!
pages.prompt: Snail beneath big village tree looking back toward distant cozy home, proud surprise.

pages.zh: 下一段是草地。瓢虫陪他走了一会儿，指出一条阴凉的小径。
pages.en: Next came the meadow. Ladybird joined him for a while and showed him a shady path.
pages.prompt: Snail and Ladybird moving along shaded miniature grass path with dew drops.

pages.zh: 草叶上的露珠亮晶晶的。走得慢，也能看见许多美丽的小东西。
pages.en: Dewdrops sparkled on the grass. Moving slowly let him notice many lovely little things.
pages.prompt: Macro wonder composition Snail gazes at sparkling dewdrops on arching grass blades.

pages.zh: 中午下起雨，他躲进干燥的树洞。“今天走不远了。”他有些着急。
pages.en: Rain began at noon. He sheltered in a dry hollow log. “I won't get far today,” he worried.
pages.prompt: Snail rests inside dry hollow log watching gentle rain outdoors, satchel beside him.

pages.zh: 他吃了点东西，等雨停。“休息不是回到起点。”他轻轻告诉自己。
pages.en: He ate a little and waited. “Resting doesn't send me back to the start,” he reminded himself.
pages.prompt: Snail eats small green leaf safely sheltered with satchel, calming posture, rain beyond opening.

pages.zh: 雨后，小路分成两条。他选了花多的一边，却走到一片陌生的菜地。
pages.en: After the rain, the path forked. He chose the flower-lined branch and reached an unfamiliar vegetable patch.
pages.prompt: Snail at vegetable patch edge looking puzzled, flowering wrong path visible behind.

pages.zh: “走错了。”小蜗牛难过地缩起触角，差一点想掉头回家。
pages.en: “I took the wrong way.” His feelers drooped. For a moment, he wanted to go home.
pages.prompt: Snail beside wordless map at garden path, drooping antennae and disappointed expression.

pages.zh: 乌龟伯伯听了他的方向，带他看地图：“回到岔路，再沿小溪走。”
pages.en: Turtle listened and checked the map with him. “Back to the fork, then follow the stream.”
pages.prompt: Adult Turtle and Snail inspect pictorial map together on flat ground, Turtle gestures creek direction.

pages.zh: 这次，他先认好路边的大石头，再出发。多走的路，变成了一次经验。
pages.en: This time, he noted a large stone by the path before setting off. His detour had taught him something.
pages.prompt: Snail identifies distinctive round landmark stone beside correct creek path, confident posture.

pages.zh: 小溪挡在前面。小蜗牛没有下水，沿岸找到一座结实的小桥。
pages.en: A stream crossed his way. Little Snail stayed out of the water and found a sturdy little bridge.
pages.prompt: Snail approaches maintained small wooden footbridge over shallow gentle stream from dry bank.

pages.zh: 过了桥，是一段长坡。他走一小段，歇一会儿，夕阳给壳镀上金边。
pages.en: Beyond the bridge was a long slope. He moved a little, rested a little, and his shell glowed in the sunset.
pages.prompt: Snail resting on broad gentle grassy hill path, warm sunset rim on chestnut shell, no cliff.

pages.zh: 夜里，他有点想家，便画下今天见到的桥，打算回去讲给奶奶听。
pages.en: That night, he missed home. He drew the bridge so he could tell Grandma about it later.
pages.prompt: Snail under safe leafy shelter sketches simple bridge on blank paper, satchel nearby, gentle moonlight.

pages.zh: 又过了几天，风里多了一点咸咸的味道。天上飞过一只白海鸥。
pages.en: A few days later, the breeze smelled a little salty. A white gull passed overhead.
pages.prompt: Snail on low coastal path notices distant white gull and wind-blown dune grass, bright day.

pages.zh: 海鸥说：“翻过前面那座沙丘，就能看见海。”小蜗牛又向前挪了一步。
pages.en: “The sea is beyond that dune,” said Gull. Little Snail moved one more step forward.
pages.prompt: Gull standing on dry sand indicates broad low dune while Snail starts gentle ascent.

pages.zh: 清晨，他越过沙丘。蓝色的大海一下铺到眼前，浪声比贝壳里的宽广得多。
pages.en: At dawn, he crested the dune. Blue sea filled his view, its waves far fuller than the sound inside the shell.
pages.prompt: Grand reveal wide sunrise ocean from safe dune top, tiny Snail foreground on dry sand, calm surf far below.

pages.zh: 小蜗牛把贝壳贴在身边，笑了。原来这么远的大海，也能从家门口的第一步走到。
pages.en: Little Snail smiled beside his seashell. Even this faraway sea had begun with one small step outside his door.
pages.prompt: Peaceful final Snail with seashell and teal satchel on dry dune overlooking blue horizon, expansive hopeful light.

title: 尺有所短，寸有所长
subtitle: 森林邮局招邮差
origin: 语出《楚辞·卜居》；本书为依据成语寓意创作的原创童话。

moral.zh: 本领是否合适，要看任务；认识自己，也欣赏别人的长处。
moral.en: A strength depends on the task. Know your own abilities and appreciate those of others.

idiomMeaning.zh: 尺有不适用的时候，寸也有能发挥作用的时候；比喻各有不足，也各有长处。
idiomMeaning.en: Even a long ruler has limits, and a short measure has uses; everyone has strengths and shortcomings.

visualAnchor: Cozy woodland post office with teal door, tan sorting shelves, plain sealed cream envelopes, cloth mailbags and pictorial route board without words. Little Giraffe has golden fur with chestnut patches, small ossicones, teal postal neckerchief and tan shoulder mailbag. Little Mouse is gray with large round ears, rust-red postal neckerchief and tiny tan satchel. Adult Owl postmaster is brown with cream face and round spectacles. Routes include high tree platform with safe railings and low root tunnel. No ladders used by tiny Mouse, no squeezed or injured characters.

pages.zh: 森林邮局缺两位邮差。长颈鹿和小老鼠，背着新邮包来试工。
pages.en: The forest post office needed two carriers. Giraffe and Mouse arrived with new mailbags for a trial day.
pages.prompt: Establish teal-door post office with Giraffe and tiny Mouse arriving, Owl welcomes them.

pages.zh: 猫头鹰局长拿出两封信：“先把它们送到收信人的手里吧。”
pages.en: Postmaster Owl handed them two letters. “Let's start by delivering these.”
pages.prompt: Owl offers two plain sealed envelopes over low sorting counter to Giraffe and Mouse.

pages.zh: 长颈鹿抬起头，轻轻一递，就把信送上了树屋的平台。
pages.en: Giraffe lifted his head and easily passed a letter to a tree-house platform.
pages.prompt: Giraffe reaches high safely railed tree platform with envelope, small recipient squirrel receives it.

pages.zh: 小老鼠走进树根下的窄道，很快把另一封信送到了洞口。
pages.en: Mouse slipped along a narrow passage under the roots and soon delivered the other letter.
pages.prompt: Mouse with satchel in cozy broad-for-mouse root passage delivering sealed envelope at burrow door.

pages.zh: 他们高高兴兴回邮局。第二轮，路线却换了。
pages.en: They returned happily. For the next round, however, their routes changed.
pages.prompt: Both return smiling to Owl who indicates two different wordless route pictures.

pages.zh: 长颈鹿来到低矮的树洞前，弯下脖子，还是进不去。
pages.en: Giraffe reached a low tree hollow. Even bending his neck, he could not fit inside.
pages.prompt: Giraffe outside low hollow entrance realizing size mismatch, head remains outside safely.

pages.zh: 小老鼠站在高树下面，仰得帽子都快掉了，仍然够不到信箱。
pages.en: Mouse looked up at a high mailbox until his cap nearly slipped, but he still could not reach it.
pages.prompt: Tiny Mouse gazes upward from safe ground at high tree mailbox, dramatic scale, small optional plain cap.

pages.zh: “我要是小一点就好了。”“我要是高一点就好了。”他们各自叹气。
pages.en: “If only I were smaller.” “If only I were taller.” Each gave a sigh.
pages.prompt: Giraffe and Mouse sit on opposite sides of post office bench, disappointed but gentle expressions.

pages.zh: 第二天，长颈鹿学小老鼠缩着身子，小老鼠学长颈鹿踮着脚尖。
pages.en: The next day, Giraffe tried to crouch like Mouse, while Mouse tried stretching as tall as Giraffe.
pages.prompt: At post office yard Giraffe awkwardly crouches and Mouse stands on tiptoe, playful harmless contrast.

pages.zh: 两个人忙了半天，反而把邮包弄歪了。“也许我不适合当邮差。”
pages.en: After all that effort, only their bags were crooked. “Maybe I'm not meant to be a carrier.”
pages.prompt: Both straighten crooked satchels beside sorting bench, Owl approaches kindly.

pages.zh: 局长没有急着回答。他拿来一封当天必须送到的信。
pages.en: The postmaster did not answer right away. He brought a letter that had to arrive that day.
pages.prompt: Owl thoughtfully presents one sealed cream envelope to both attentive carriers.

pages.zh: 送信的路，要先经过高树平台，再穿过低低的树根通道。
pages.en: The route led over a high tree platform and then through a low passage under the roots.
pages.prompt: Single wide geographic scene shows high accessible tree platform connected by gentle path to low root passage, no split panels.

pages.zh: 长颈鹿看看小老鼠：“高处我能送。”小老鼠抬起头：“后半程交给我！”
pages.en: Giraffe looked at Mouse. “I can handle the high part.” Mouse replied, “Leave the last part to me!”
pages.prompt: Two carriers agree to cooperate beside route board with simple unlettered shapes.

pages.zh: 长颈鹿先把信递上平台，管理员再从另一侧的小篮子里放下来。
pages.en: Giraffe passed the letter up to the platform. Its keeper lowered it on the other side in a small basket.
pages.prompt: Giraffe passes envelope to squirrel keeper at safe railed platform with small rope basket on far side.

pages.zh: 小老鼠接过信，沿着树根通道，一路送到山坡另一边。
pages.en: Mouse took the letter through the root passage to the other side of the hill.
pages.prompt: Mouse takes cream envelope from safely lowered basket then faces cozy root tunnel entrance.

pages.zh: 收信人笑着打开门：“谢谢你们，正好赶上！”
pages.en: The recipient opened the door with a smile. “Thank you both. Just in time!”
pages.prompt: Mouse delivers letter to rabbit recipient at hillside burrow door, Giraffe visible along outer path afar.

pages.zh: 回到邮局，局长按路线分好任务。他们不再比赛谁能做所有的事。
pages.en: Back at the post office, Owl assigned routes to suit them. They stopped competing to do everything.
pages.prompt: Owl sorts letters into high and low accessible shelves while both carriers receive matching assignments.

pages.zh: 长颈鹿低下头，小老鼠举起爪，轻轻碰了一下。尺有所短，寸有所长，好搭档各有本领。
pages.en: Giraffe bent down and Mouse raised a paw for a gentle greeting. Different strengths made them a good team.
pages.prompt: Final Giraffe bends gently so tiny Mouse can touch his muzzle with paw, warm post office backdrop.

title: 一叶障目，不见泰山
subtitle: 小松鼠找大山
origin: 相关语句见《鹖冠子·天则》；本书为成语寓意改编的原创童话，并非原典故事。

moral.zh: 看见一部分时，先别急着下结论；换个位置，听听别人，再一起观察。
moral.en: Before drawing a conclusion from one small part, change viewpoints and compare observations.

idiomMeaning.zh: 一片叶子挡住眼睛，就看不见大山；比喻被局部或表面现象蒙蔽，看不到整体。
idiomMeaning.en: A leaf can hide a mountain from view; a narrow view can keep us from seeing the whole.

visualAnchor: Peaceful Chinese-inspired wooded valley with enormous distant blue-gray mountain, meadow clearing and broad safe paths. Little Squirrel is russet with cream belly and large fluffy tail, teal cap and mustard artist satchel. Rabbit friend is white with lavender scarf. Adult Owl teacher has warm brown feathers, cream face and round spectacles. Fixed large green sycamore leaf held close to eye, small wooden drawing board, blank cream drawing paper and simple natural-color crayons. Mountain is genuinely enormous but hidden by nearby foliage or framing; no magical shrinking.

pages.zh: 小松鼠第一次来山脚画画。他背着画板，想画一座大大的山。
pages.en: Little Squirrel came to the foothills to draw for the first time. He wanted to paint a great mountain.
pages.prompt: Squirrel arrives on broad wooded valley path carrying drawing board, distant mountain partly hidden by trees.

pages.zh: 路边有一片漂亮的大叶子，叶脉像细细的小路。小松鼠一下看入了迷。
pages.en: A beautiful leaf caught his eye. Its veins looked like tiny paths, and he was fascinated.
pages.prompt: Squirrel studies large green sycamore leaf in close-up, fine natural veins visible.

pages.zh: 他把叶子举到眼前，左看看，右看看。满眼都是绿绿的一片。
pages.en: He held the leaf right before his eyes. Looking left and right, all he could see was green.
pages.prompt: Side view leaf held very close to Squirrel's eyes, blocks line of sight toward mountain beyond.

pages.zh: 小兔指着远处：“看，那就是大山！”小松鼠摇头：“哪里有山？”
pages.en: Rabbit pointed into the distance. “Look, there's the mountain!” “What mountain?” Squirrel asked.
pages.prompt: Rabbit gestures toward large mountain while Squirrel still holds leaf across own eyes.

pages.zh: 他举着叶子转来转去，最后宣布：“这里只有树叶，根本没有大山！”
pages.en: He turned around with the leaf still raised. “There's only a leaf here. There isn't any mountain!”
pages.prompt: Squirrel confidently gestures with free paw, leaf remains before face; Rabbit looks puzzled.

pages.zh: 小兔笑着请他放下叶子。叶子一移开，远处露出了一角青色的山。
pages.en: Rabbit asked him to lower it. As the leaf moved, a blue corner of the mountain appeared.
pages.prompt: Squirrel lowers leaf partially, mountain peak emerges beyond foreground foliage, surprise.

pages.zh: 可小松鼠又钻到树洞口，从窄窄的缝里看。“山原来只有这么一点！”
pages.en: Then Squirrel peered through a narrow hollow. “So the mountain is only this tiny bit!”
pages.prompt: Squirrel peers through narrow tree hollow opening from safe ground, limited slice of mountain framed.

pages.zh: 他在纸上画了个小尖角，得意地举起来。小兔的画，却宽得占满了纸。
pages.en: He proudly drew a little point. Rabbit's mountain, however, filled the whole page.
pages.prompt: Squirrel and Rabbit compare wordless drawings small triangular tip versus broad mountain silhouette.

pages.zh: “我们画的，怎么不一样？”小松鼠皱起眉头。
pages.en: “Why are our pictures different?” Squirrel frowned.
pages.prompt: Close emotional scene friends compare differing mountain drawings, Squirrel puzzled rather than arguing.

pages.zh: 猫头鹰老师走来，没有替他们改画，而是请他们说说自己站在哪里。
pages.en: Owl came over. Instead of fixing the pictures, she asked where each of them had stood.
pages.prompt: Adult Owl listens to both young artists describing viewpoints beside tree and meadow.

pages.zh: 小松鼠指指树洞，小兔指指草地。原来，他们看到的范围不同。
pages.en: Squirrel pointed to the hollow and Rabbit to the meadow. They had seen different amounts of the same view.
pages.prompt: Wide continuous scene shows tree hollow foreground and open meadow nearby with broad mountain beyond.

pages.zh: 老师带他们退到空地上。山脚、山腰和山顶，渐渐连成了一整座山。
pages.en: Owl led them into the clearing. The foot, slopes, and summit joined into one whole mountain.
pages.prompt: Three characters on open clearing facing full massive blue-gray mountain with foot slopes summit visible.

pages.zh: 小松鼠张大嘴：“大山一直都在，是我刚才没看全！”
pages.en: Squirrel's mouth fell open. “The mountain was here all along. I just couldn't see all of it!”
pages.prompt: Squirrel amazed in foreground with lowered leaf, full mountain expansively behind, warm revelation.

pages.zh: 他又把叶子举起来试一试。小小一片叶，靠得太近，真能挡住大山。
pages.en: He tried holding up the leaf again. A little leaf, held close enough, really could hide a mountain.
pages.prompt: Profile composition demonstrates leaf close to Squirrel face obscures distant mountain along gaze, Owl observes.

pages.zh: 这次，他先放下叶子，左右走走，再仔细看山的轮廓。
pages.en: This time, he lowered the leaf, moved around, and studied the mountain's outline.
pages.prompt: Squirrel explores open clearing with board under arm and leaf held low, mountain fully visible.

pages.zh: 他也听小兔说起山脚的小溪，听老师指出云下面的另一道山坡。
pages.en: He listened as Rabbit described the stream below and Owl pointed out another slope beneath the clouds.
pages.prompt: Rabbit points toward stream and Owl toward mountain slope, Squirrel listens with drawing board.

pages.zh: 新画纸上，大山舒展开来。那片漂亮的叶子，被他画在了近处。
pages.en: On a fresh sheet, the mountain stretched wide. He painted the lovely leaf in the foreground.
pages.prompt: Close view Squirrel creating coherent painting with broad mountain and small foreground leaf, no letters.

pages.zh: 小松鼠把两张画放在一起：“下次看见一点点，我会先问，还有什么没看见？”
pages.en: Squirrel placed both pictures together. “Next time I see a little, I'll ask what else I might be missing.”
pages.prompt: Final friends compare earlier tiny-peak sketch with complete mountain-and-leaf painting in sunny clearing.

title: 八仙过海，各显神通
subtitle: 不用大船的渡海之旅
origin: 中国民间传说“八仙过海”的温和改编；法宝及渡海细节在不同讲述中有所差异，本书省略龙宫争斗。

moral.zh: 面对同一件事，可以有不同办法；发挥所长，也别忘了照应同行的人。
moral.en: One task can have many solutions. Use your strengths and look out for others along the way.

idiomMeaning.zh: 八位仙人各用法宝渡海；比喻各自拿出本领，解决问题或完成任务。
idiomMeaning.en: The Eight Immortals each use a special skill to cross the sea; people can solve a task in different ways.

visualAnchor: Gentle Chinese Eight Immortals legend on bright calm turquoise sea between safe sandy shores; all are clearly adult magical figures with distinct fixed designs. Tieguai Li: sturdy older man, dark curly beard, messy topknot, brown patched robe, iron walking staff, ochre double-gourd. Han Zhongli: cheerful stocky bald-crowned man with two side buns, short beard, loose pale-mint robe over cream inner tunic, large green banana-leaf fan. He Xiangu: graceful woman, dark high bun, peach-pink hanfu, cream sash, large pink lotus. Lan Caihe: youthful adult, short tousled hair, teal robe, woven flower basket. Zhang Guolao: elderly man, long white beard, white hair bun, lavender robe, bamboo fish-drum tube. Han Xiangzi: young adult clean-shaven man, neat black bun, indigo robe, jade flute. Cao Guojiu: middle-aged clean-shaven man, maroon robe, simple dark ceremonial cap, pair of pale jade clappers. Lu Dongbin: middle-aged man with black moustache and small beard, cream robe, blue sash, dark scholar cap, fully sheathed sword strapped behind back. Magical props enlarge to form wide stable floating supports; no ordinary people imitating, no battle, no weapons unsheathed. Depict only named characters in each page scene; all eight only when requested.

pages.zh: 传说，有八位仙人结伴出游。一天，他们来到蓝蓝的大海边。
pages.en: In a legend, eight immortals traveled together. One day, they reached a bright blue sea.
pages.prompt: Wide establishing sandy shore with all eight fixed adult immortals in distinct costumes, calm turquoise sea.

pages.zh: 远处的小岛像一片青叶。吕洞宾说：“今天，我们不用大船，怎样过去呢？”
pages.en: A distant island looked like a green leaf. “How shall we get there without a large boat?” asked Lü Dongbin.
pages.prompt: Lu Dongbin in cream robe gestures toward distant green island, Han Zhongli and He Xiangu beside him.

pages.zh: 汉钟离摇摇扇子：“各用各的法宝，各想各的办法！”大家笑着点头。
pages.en: Han Zhongli waved his fan. “Let's each use our own magic and find our own way!” The others agreed.
pages.prompt: Han Zhongli holds green fan cheerfully while Tieguai Li and Lan Caihe nod beside him on shore.

pages.zh: 铁拐李先放下葫芦。葫芦迎风变大，稳稳浮在水面上，像一只圆圆的小船。
pages.en: Tieguai Li set down his gourd. It grew in the breeze and floated like a round little boat.
pages.prompt: Tieguai Li beside magically enlarged ochre double-gourd floating stably at calm shoreline, iron staff visible.

pages.zh: 他坐好后，葫芦轻轻向前，身后留下一道弯弯的水纹。
pages.en: Once he was seated, the gourd glided ahead, leaving a curling trail on the water.
pages.prompt: Tieguai Li securely seated on wide magical gourd, brown robe and staff unchanged, curved wake.

pages.zh: 汉钟离把芭蕉扇往水上一放。大扇子铺开，托着他悠悠前行。
pages.en: Han Zhongli laid his banana-leaf fan on the water. It spread wide and carried him gently along.
pages.prompt: Han Zhongli on enlarged stable green banana fan on calm sea, mint robe and side buns clear.

pages.zh: 何仙姑托起荷花。粉红花瓣舒展开来，像一座柔软的小亭子。
pages.en: He Xiangu raised her lotus. Its pink petals opened into a soft little pavilion.
pages.prompt: He Xiangu securely seated inside broad pink lotus with petal sides, peach hanfu, tranquil water.

pages.zh: 蓝采和放下花篮，篮子变得宽宽的。一路花香，随着海风轻轻飘散。
pages.en: Lan Caihe lowered a flower basket, which grew broad and roomy. Its fragrance drifted with the sea breeze.
pages.prompt: Lan Caihe seated inside enlarged high-sided woven flower basket floating magically, teal robe, colorful blossoms.

pages.zh: 张果老拍拍渔鼓。长长的竹筒变成稳稳的浮筏，托着白胡子爷爷出发了。
pages.en: Zhang Guolao tapped his bamboo drum. It became a steady floating raft and carried the white-bearded elder away.
pages.prompt: Zhang Guolao in lavender robe seated securely on magically broadened bamboo fish-drum raft, long white beard.

pages.zh: 韩湘子吹了声笛，玉笛便化作碧绿的长舟，滑过清亮的海水。
pages.en: Han Xiangzi played a note. His jade flute became a slender green boat that glided across the clear water.
pages.prompt: Han Xiangzi in indigo robe seated safely in broad enough jade-flute-shaped magical boat, gentle ripples.

pages.zh: 曹国舅把两片玉板轻轻一合。玉板化成小艇，平平稳稳向前走。
pages.en: Cao Guojiu brought his jade clappers together. They became a little craft that moved steadily forward.
pages.prompt: Cao Guojiu in maroon robe and ceremonial cap seated securely on paired pale-jade clapper craft with raised sides.

pages.zh: 吕洞宾的宝剑仍收在鞘里。他轻点剑鞘，剑鞘化成宽舟，载着他跟上伙伴。
pages.en: Lü Dongbin kept his sword sheathed. At his touch, the sheath became a broad vessel, carrying him after his friends.
pages.prompt: Lu Dongbin in cream robe blue sash seated on wide magical sheathed-sword vessel, blade never visible.

pages.zh: 海面上，八种法宝留下八道水纹。快慢不同，谁也没有催谁。
pages.en: Eight magical vessels left eight trails across the sea. They moved at different speeds, and nobody hurried anyone.
pages.prompt: High wide view exactly eight distinct magical vessels and fixed immortals spaced comfortably on calm sea, eight wakes.

pages.zh: 走到半途，海风换了方向。蓝采和的花篮轻轻偏向一边。
pages.en: Halfway across, the breeze changed. Lan Caihe's flower basket drifted gently to one side.
pages.prompt: Lan Caihe in stable roomy flower basket gently drifts off course, petals tilt with mild breeze, no danger.

pages.zh: “往这边看！”铁拐李指着小岛。蓝采和认准方向，慢慢调正花篮。
pages.en: “Look this way!” Tieguai Li pointed toward the island. Lan Caihe turned the basket back on course.
pages.prompt: Tieguai Li on gourd points island direction toward Lan Caihe adjusting stable basket, calm spacing.

pages.zh: 汉钟离没有猛扇，只轻轻送来一阵顺风。何仙姑也放慢荷花，陪在旁边。
pages.en: Han Zhongli sent only a gentle guiding breeze. He Xiangu slowed her lotus to stay beside them.
pages.prompt: Han Zhongli on fan uses gentle magical breeze, He Xiangu in lotus accompanies Lan Caihe in basket, three figures only.

pages.zh: 张果老和韩湘子看见前面的浅滩，提醒大家绕开露出水面的礁石。
pages.en: Zhang Guolao and Han Xiangzi noticed a shallow patch and warned everyone to steer around the visible rocks.
pages.prompt: Zhang Guolao on bamboo raft and Han Xiangzi on flute boat point away from distant visible low rocks, wide safe channel.

pages.zh: 八位仙人依次靠岸，把法宝收好。蓝采和笑着说：“多谢一路照应！”
pages.en: One by one, the immortals reached shore and gathered their treasures. “Thank you for looking out for me,” said Lan Caihe.
pages.prompt: All eight fixed adults safely on sandy island shore beside their distinct props returning to handheld size.

pages.zh: 大家坐在树荫下，说起各自的办法。原来，同一片海，可以这样走，也可以那样走。
pages.en: Sitting in the shade, they shared their different ways of traveling. The same sea could be crossed in many ways.
pages.prompt: Eight immortals relaxed under broad island tree showing original handheld props, calm ocean behind, sword fully sheathed.

pages.zh: 八仙过海，各显神通。海风吹过，八道不同的水纹，慢慢汇进同一片蓝色里。
pages.en: Each immortal had used a different gift. In the breeze, their eight trails slowly blended into the same blue sea.
pages.prompt: Closing panoramic calm blue sea with eight gentle fading wakes toward island where tiny eight figures rest, poetic sunset.
